guidance: The layout is a ring: the two series arms of Z0 divided by the square root of two run along the through path and the two Z0 arms bridge across it. Every arm is a quarter wave at the design frequency, so shorten each one by the excess the T-junction adds in your simulator, and take the substrate, copper and etch data from the laminate datasheet.
method: A single-section branch-line hybrid is a ring of four quarter-wave lines: the two series arms that join ports 1-2 and 3-4 are Z0 divided by the square root of two and the two shunt arms that join ports 2-3 and 4-1 are Z0, so a 50 ohm system uses 35.355 ohm and 50 ohm lines and a 75 ohm system uses 53.033 ohm and 75 ohm. Each arm is 90 electrical degrees at the design frequency, so its physical length is a quarter of the guided wavelength, lambda_g = c v_f / f with c = 299792458 m/s. At the design point the network is matched, the input splits equally, the through port 2 is the phase reference and the coupled port 3 lags it by 90 degrees while port 4 is isolated. Away from the design frequency the four-port response comes from the nodal admittance matrix of the four ideal lines: a line of impedance Z and electrical length theta contributes y11 = -j cot(theta)/Z and y12 = j csc(theta)/Z between its two nodes, and with every port terminated in Z0 the scattering matrix is S = (I - Z0 Y)(I + Z0 Y)^-1, evaluated by complex Gauss-Jordan elimination. Return loss is -20 log10 |S11| and isolation is -20 log10 |S41|, both capped at 60 dB because the model is lossless. The 20 dB bandwidth is the contiguous span around the design frequency over which both the return loss and the isolation stay at or above 20 dB, its edges located by bisection so the result does not depend on a scan step. Inputs are limited to a system impedance of 5 to 1000 ohms, a design frequency of 0.1 to 40000 MHz, a velocity factor of 0.3 to 1 and an analysis frequency of 0.2 to 1.8 times the design frequency; text, empty values and out-of-range numbers are refused with the field named. Warnings appear for a return loss below 10 dB at the analysis frequency, an arm shorter than 1 mm, a shunt arm above 120 ohms and a series arm below 20 ohms. The junction discontinuity, dispersion, conductor and dielectric loss and fabrication tolerance are not modelled, so a real coupler needs an electromagnetic simulation or a measured prototype.

sources.title: Microwaves101, Branchline Couplers: every transmission line is a quarter wavelength, the signal at port 1 splits into quadrature signals at ports 2 and 3, and port 4 is isolated at the centre frequency.
